Q: What is this sub about?

A: This sub is meant to be like /r/lurkers. The joke over in /r/ was that there were 8000 subscribers and no posts. Everyone instinctively knew not to post because the joke is that lurkers don't but they might still be there, pass through, check the tabs. Here, we will have lurkers, no posts, and a lot of mods - kind of a comment on surveillance, who's watching who, and why we lurk(ed) in the first place when practically speaking, there's nothing to see. You can think of it as a commentary, satire and performance art piece on domestic surveillance and free speech, in that we would all be participating by not participating and that hopefully everyone who subscribed would also be a mod, ostensibly watching, though there is obviously no work involved.

This sub is still in its infancy, but we envision that one day it will be an old sub with a huge number of subscribers, a long list of mods, and no posts. So feel free to spread the word and subscribe - and if you want to be a mod, PM /u/ack.

I'm confused, is this talking about an embedded SIM card or a SIM card that allows you to connect to any carrier? Or an embedded SIM card that allows you to connect to any carrier?

Remember the old CDMA handsets that you had to call the carrier and read them the ESN off the back of the phone? Then they would verify the handset is not currently attached to another account/stolen/etc. and that it will work with their network, after which, they will register that device to your account (for a fee)?

it'll be like that.

The traditional Sim card locks in the user to a network but an embedded Sim would enable a smartphone, tablet or wearable user to avoid locking themselves into a plan with a single operator or sign up to switch instantly.

....Uh, that's actually the exact opposite of true. The SIM is not what locks the device to the carrier, the carrier lock is on the phone itself.

Currently, SIM cards can be swapped to use a different network, whereas (as on the CDMA networks of old) under this 'e-sim' system, it would be reverted to having to beg the carrier to pretty please unlock your phone from one network/plan, and then activate it on another.

While I am sure it would be great as an anti-theft measure, since the phone would be useless unless first unlocked from your account, it is FAR from being more convenient than the current SIM system.
